service_boundary: Represents the Gemini API reached through Google AI Studio credentials, not Gemini Apps, Vertex AI, individual Gemini releases, or Google Cloud-hosted partner models.
regional_controls: The direct API is a global developer service; customer-selected Google Cloud regions and residency controls belong to the separate Vertex AI boundary.
retention_controls: Data use and logging depend on whether access is through paid services and on enabled features; customers must review the current Gemini API additional terms and feature-specific storage behavior.
routing: Customers select models from Google's direct catalog; this is not a cross-provider router.
customization: The reviewed direct API supports prompting, caching, files, tools, and tuned-model features where documented, not customer-managed serving infrastructure.
strengths: Direct access to Google's multimodal model APIs and developer tooling.
Native and OpenAI-compatible integration paths are documented.
tradeoffs: Its governance boundary differs from Vertex AI.
Feature availability and data behavior vary across free, paid, and stateful features.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the model appears in the API reference; the thinking guide's "thought signatures" are opaque tokens for carrying reasoning state between turns, not a client-verifiable signature of the response.
response_integrity.scope: Gemini API thinking guide, read for response verification, for the Gemini API

upstream_disclosure.note: The logs policy states how Google handles API content, including that "Human reviewers may read, annotate, and process the API inputs and outputs you share." on the unpaid tier; the operator is the party that receives plaintext.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Gemini API logs policy, for the Gemini API

credential_handling.note: The API offers no customer-supplied-key path: "Google AI Studio automatically creates a default Google Cloud project and API key after you accept the Terms of Service." and every documented request uses that key.
credential_handling.scope: Gemini API key guide, for the Gemini API

cache_isolation.note: The context-caching guide documents explicit and implicit caching, their pricing, and their lifetimes, but never states whether a cache is scoped to the project or key that created it or can be reached from another customer's requests.
cache_isolation.scope: Gemini API context-caching guide, for the Gemini API

vulnerability_disclosure.note: Google publishes a company-wide security.txt with a disclosure route ("Contact: https://g.co/vulnz" and "Contact: mailto:security@google.com"), and its Bug Hunters site carries an AI vulnerability reward programme covering Google AI products; neither names the Gemini API specifically.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Google security.txt, for the Gemini API

independent_audit.note: The Google Cloud SOC 2 page ("Below are Google Cloud services that are in scope for SOC 2.") lists the in-scope services and does not name the Gemini API or Google AI Studio, and no AI Studio compliance page was found; recorded as undocumented for the named service.
independent_audit.scope: Google Cloud SOC 2 scope page, read for the Gemini API
